quote: Andrew M. Gleason made this reasoning explicit, conjecturing there are infinitely many Pierpont primes, and more specifically that there should be approximately 9n Pierpont primes up to 10ⁿ.
note: The conjecture was posed in Gleason's 1988 paper in the American Mathematical Monthly, Vol. 95, No. 3, pp. 185–194, which made explicit the reasoning that there should be infinitely many Pierpont primes.
